skill.name: telegram-automation
skill.description: Automate Telegram bot workflows through Rube MCP, including messages, media, chat management, updates, and bot commands.
skill.summary: Guide Telegram bot automation through Rube MCP tool workflows.
skill.author: sickn33

security_audit.summary: Most static external-command and system-reconnaissance findings are false positives from Markdown code spans around Telegram tool names and parameters. The skill does require a third-party Rube MCP endpoint and documents sensitive Telegram actions, including sending, deleting, forwarding, and reading chats. No prompt injection or covert malware behavior was found in SKILL.md.

remediation.issue: Third-party MCP server handles Telegram automation.
remediation.suggestion: Document what data Rube MCP can access and require explicit user approval before connecting the Telegram bot.

remediation.issue: The workflows include sensitive Telegram actions.
remediation.suggestion: Require confirmation before sending, deleting, forwarding, exporting invite links, or reading chat history.

remediation.issue: Markdown tool names resemble executable commands to static scanners.
remediation.suggestion: Clarify that the named TELEGRAM_* and RUBE_* items are MCP tool calls, not shell commands.

static_findings.snippet: - Active Telegram connection via `RUBE_MANAGE_CONNECTIONS` with toolkit `telegram`
- Always call `RUBE_SEARCH_TOOLS` first to get current tool schemas
**Get Rube MCP**: Add `https://rube.app/mcp` as an MCP server in your client configuration. No API k
1. Verify Rube MCP is available by confirming `RUBE_SEARCH_TOOLS` responds
2. `TELEGRAM_GET_CHAT` - Get chat details and verify access [Optional]
- `chat_id`: Numeric chat ID or channel username (e.g., '@channelname')
- `chat_id`: Chat where the message is located
- `message_id`: ID of the message to edit or delete
1. `TELEGRAM_FORWARD_MESSAGE` - Forward a message to another chat [Optional]
- `commands`: Array of command objects with `command` and `description`
- `callback_query_id`: ID of the callback query to answer
**Get Rube MCP**: Add `https://rube.app/mcp` as an MCP server in your client configuration. No API k
- Use offset to avoid processing the same update twice
1. Use '@username' format as chat_id (for public channels/groups)
2. For private chats, numeric chat_id is required
3. Use numeric chat_id in subsequent calls
| Forward message | TELEGRAM_FORWARD_MESSAGE | chat_id, from_chat_id, message_id |

semantic_findings.title: Sensitive Telegram Operations Require Confirmation
semantic_findings.description: The skill documents workflows that can send, edit, delete, forward, export invite links, retrieve updates, and access chat history. These actions can expose private chat data or alter conversations if used without clear user approval.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The listed workflows explicitly cover message sending, destructive message actions, invite link export, updates, and chat history. These are legitimate Telegram features, but they are sensitive business-logic actions.

content.value_statement: Managing Telegram bots across chats can require many exact API calls. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through Rube MCP workflows.
actual_capabilities: Connects Telegram bot workflows through Rube MCP tool discovery.
Sends text messages with plain text, HTML, or MarkdownV2 formatting.
Shares photos and documents by URL or Telegram file_id.
Retrieves chat details, administrators, member counts, updates, and chat history when permitted.
Edits, deletes, and forwards messages when bot permissions allow.
Sets bot commands and answers callback queries.
limitations: Requires Rube MCP access and an active Telegram bot connection.
Cannot bypass Telegram bot permissions or chat membership rules.
Bots cannot initiate private conversations with users.
Telegram rate limits, message limits, and file size limits still apply.

use_cases.title: Send Community Updates
use_cases.description: Prepare and send formatted announcements to Telegram groups or channels with the correct chat identifier.

use_cases.title: Manage Support Chats
use_cases.description: Check chat details, forward messages, and keep bot command menus aligned with support workflows.

use_cases.title: Build Bot Workflows
use_cases.description: Use Rube MCP tool discovery to test message, media, callback, and update flows for a Telegram bot.

prompt_templates.title: Send a Basic Message
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the Telegram automation skill to send this message to chat {chat_id}: {message}. Verify the bot identity first.

prompt_templates.title: Share Media With Caption
prompt_templates.prompt: Send {media_url_or_file_id} to Telegram chat {chat_id} with this caption: {caption}. Use the right photo or document workflow.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Chat Access
prompt_templates.prompt: Check Telegram chat {chat_id}, summarize available chat details, list administrators if permitted, and explain any missing permissions.

prompt_templates.title: Maintain Bot Commands
prompt_templates.prompt: Review the current Telegram bot command needs for {workflow}. Create a safe command list and update the bot menu through Rube MCP.

output_examples.input: Send a release note to the product updates channel.
output_examples.output: Bot identity checked, channel access confirmed, release note sent with the requested formatting, and message limits verified.

output_examples.input: Find the chat ID from recent bot updates.
output_examples.output: Recent updates reviewed, the matching chat was identified, and the numeric chat ID was provided for future approved actions.

output_examples.input: Update the bot command menu for a support bot.
output_examples.output: Command names were normalized, descriptions were checked for length, and the bot command list was replaced after confirmation.

best_practices: Verify bot identity and target chat before any send, edit, delete, or forward action.
Use the least privileged bot permissions needed for each Telegram workflow.
Respect Telegram rate limits and split long messages before sending.
anti_patterns: Do not send messages to a chat ID that the user has not confirmed.
Do not export invite links or read chat history without explicit approval.
Do not assume MarkdownV2 formatting is safe without escaping special characters.

faq.question: What does this skill automate?
faq.answer: It guides Telegram bot actions through Rube MCP, including messages, media, chat details, updates, and bot commands.

faq.question: Does it need a Telegram bot token?
faq.answer: Yes. The Telegram bot must be configured through Rube MCP before workflows can run.

faq.question: Can it message any Telegram user?
faq.answer: No. Telegram bots cannot start private chats, and they must have access to the target chat.

faq.question: Can it delete messages?
faq.answer: Yes, when Telegram permissions and timing rules allow it. Users should confirm delete actions first.

faq.question: Why does it search tools first?
faq.answer: Rube MCP tool schemas can change, so the skill checks current parameters before calling Telegram tools.

faq.question: Is chat history access always available?
faq.answer: No. Chat history depends on bot permissions, chat type, and what Telegram exposes to the bot.
